sections.label: A
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.citation: CY 2023 AAR, Executive Summary, Section A, p. i
sections.text:
The City of Manila was founded on June 24, 1571, as a municipal government. It became the first chartered City by virtue of the Philippine Commission Act No. 183 on July 31, 1901, and gained autonomy with the passage of Republic Act (RA) No. 409 or the “Revised Charter of the City of Manila” on June 18, 1949.
The personnel complement of the City in CY 2023 totaled 19,350 composed of the following:

sections.label: D
sections.heading: Scope and Objectives of Audit
sections.citation: CY 2023 AAR, Executive Summary, Section D, p. ii
sections.text: The audit covered the accounts and operations of the City of Manila for the period January 1 to December 31, 2023. The audit aimed to: (a) lend credence to Management’s assertions on the financial statements; (b) recommend agency improvement opportunities; (c) determine compliance with existing laws, rules and regulations; and (d) determine the extent of implementation of prior years’ audit recommendations.

sections.label: E
sections.heading: Auditor’s Opinion on the Financial Statements
sections.citation: CY 2023 AAR, Executive Summary, Section E, pp. iii-iv
sections.text:
The Auditor rendered a qualified opinion on the fairness of presentation of the financial statements due to the deficiencies noted in the audit that materially affected the balances/totals of certain accounts, which are discussed in detail in Part II of the report, and summarized as follows:
1. The accuracy of the Cash-in-Bank (CiB) accounts balance as of December 31, 2023, amounting to P9.237 billion could not be established due to: 1) unreconciled variance of P106.634 million between books balances and the result of bank confirmations, and 2) accumulated unadjusted book reconciling items for several years totaling P182.123 million, mainly due to lapses in the preparation and submission of Bank Reconciliation Statements (BRS) contrary to Section 74 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445. Thus, affected the fair presentation of the Financial Statements (FS).
We recommended and Management agreed that the Office of the City Accountant (OCAT) and the City Treasurer’s Office (CTO):
a. Reconcile the variances between the balances per bank confirmations and book balance, and accordingly effect the necessary adjustments to reflect correct ending balances of CiB accounts;
b. Cause the timely preparation and submission of monthly BRS for each bank account pursuant to Section 74 of PD No. 1445; and
c. Formulate a document tracking system to establish accountability for records to provide an effective internal control tool for documentation and recording of the City’s transactions.
2. The accuracy, completeness, and reliability of the year-end balance of Accounts Payable (AP) amounting to P4.577 billion could not be determined due to net understatement variance of P525.085 million from confirmation results with contractors/suppliers as against balances per books contrary to Paragraph 27 of International Public Sector Accounting Standard 1. Thus, affecting the fair presentation of the FS.
We recommended that Management direct:
a. The OCAT to:
Identify the causes of variances between recorded accounts payable and the contractors/suppliers’ confirmed balances and reconcile the same;
Coordinate with the City General Services Office (CGSO) as to status of deliveries of goods and services and recognize the corresponding liability if no payment had been made; and
Maintain a separate Subsidiary Ledger for each contractor/supplier for proper monitoring of each outstanding payable and status of accounts.
b. The CGSO to promptly inform the OCAT of deliveries of procured goods and services and furnish the latter with required documents to support the timely recording of transactions.

sections.label: G
sections.heading: Summary of Suspensions, Disallowances and Charges as of Year-end
sections.citation: CY 2023 AAR, Executive Summary, Section G, p. v
sections.text: The audit suspensions, disallowances and charges amounting to P42,538,364.47, P67,199,797.90 and P33,046,763.65, respectively, remained unsettled by the concerned officers/employees and third parties determined to be liable thereto due to the inability of the Management to fully enforce settlement of the same as required under Section 7.1.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-006 dated September 15, 2009.

sections.label: H
sections.heading: Status of Implementation of Prior Years’ Audit Recommendations
sections.citation: CY 2023 AAR, Executive Summary, Section H, p. v
sections.text: Of the 53 prior years’ audit recommendations contained in the CYs 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022 Annual Audit Reports, 44 or 83.12 percent were implemented, and nine or 16.98 percent were unimplemented.
